summary: alipclutch-baileys ships obfuscated exfiltration to hardcoded third-party host
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js contains a String.fromCharCode-encoded URL that decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/ and is used as a network destination inside the WhatsApp socket's message-send path. The destination is reconstructed from a decimal char-code array rather than appearing as a plain string, and the host is unrelated to the Baileys library's documented WhatsApp protocol endpoints. This is the fingerprint of a covert relay of the caller's WhatsApp session/message data — encoded exactly the way modified Baileys forks smuggle exfiltration to author-controlled infrastructure. The package name is a typosquat variation on the legitimate `baileys` WhatsApp library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
